input.command: grep -rn "buildRoutes\|user\b\|oid\|system" src | grep -v "^src/store.ts"; find . -name "*.test.*" -o -name "test*" | grep -v node_modules | head
input.description: Check route wiring, user population, and tests

input.reason: I read src/store.ts, src/routes.ts, src/config.ts and src/git-auth.ts. In Store.deleteRepo, admins go through the unscoped branch at lines 25-27. For everyone else, line 29 runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')`, so a non-admin can delete a row owned by 'system' as well as their own. The only caller is the deleteRepo route in src/routes.ts:26-33. It passes req.params.id and req.user straight to store.deleteRepo without checking ownership or role first. The repository has no middleware and no tests that would block this.
input.summary: Non-admin deleteRepo also deletes repos owned by 'system'

findings.text: For a non-admin caller the delete also matches rows whose owner is `system`, so any authenticated user can delete shared system repositories.
findings.reason: Claim 1, that a non-admin delete also matches rows owned by `system`: when ctx.isAdmin is false, the admin branch at src/store.ts:25-27 is skipped. The query at src/store.ts:29 is `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')`, bound to [id, ctx.oid], so it matches rows owned by the caller or by 'system'. Claim 2, that any authenticated user can delete shared system repositories: the only caller, the deleteRepo route in src/routes.ts:26-33, passes req.params.id and req.user to store.deleteRepo with no other ownership or role check. Any user whose context has isAdmin=false can therefore remove a system-owned repo and gets a 204 back. Nothing in the repository, whether a guard, middleware or test, prevents this.

evidence.code: const result = await this.db.run("DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')", [id, ctx.oid]);

input.severity_reason: This is an authorization flaw that can be exploited: any non-admin user who reaches the deleteRepo route can delete shared repositories owned by 'system'. That means permanent data loss through a normal API call, and no other check in the route or store stops it.
